sentences.text: The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Mummineni Sudheer Kumar

Contempt Case No.387 Of 2017
Order:
Heard Sri Ashok Anand Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 4.
Though, notice is served on respondent Nos.3 and 4 no appearance is entered on their behalf.
2. This Contempt Case is filed for the alleged violation of the orders passed by this Court in Writ Petition No.32684 of 2016 dated 27.09.2016 as extended by an order dated 26.10.2016.

By the said order, dated 27.09.2016, this Court has directed the parties to maintain status-quo as regards payment of compensation in respect of the subject property i.e., land admeasuring Ac.3.22 guntas and Ac.0.12 guntas situated in Sy. Nos.532 and 678 respectively of Vemulghat Village, Thogata Mandal, Medak District including the house property bearing House No.4-2 of Vemulghat Village.

3. It is alleged in the affidavit filed in support of the Contempt Case that the order dated 27.09.2016 passed by this Court was communicated to the respondent No.2 by the 2 MSK,J C.C.No.387 OF 2017 petitioner by submitting a representation dated 29.09.2016 and inspite of the same, the respondent No.2 has paid the compensation in favour of respondent Nos.3 and 4 on 05.10.2016 through cheques basing on the sale deeds executed by the respondent Nos.3 and 4 vide document Nos.7016 of 2016 and 7018 of 2016 dated 05.10.2016.
4.

In response to the notice issued by this Court, the respondent No.2 herein has filed counter affidavit stating that the compensation payable in respect of the subject land was already paid on 15.09.2016 i.e., much prior to the date of passing of the order by this Court on 27.09.2016 and the relevant paragraph from the counter affidavit reads as under:
"It is submitted that execution of the registered sale deeds under GOMS No.123,
dated 30.07.2013, registered their lands in favour of proposed Mallannasagar Project as per orders in appeal case vide No.D/2646/2015 of Appellate Authority i.e., the RDO, Siddipet, by the Respondent Nos.3 and 4 in Sy.No.758, 678 (0-17) gts and 532,758, 834 (4-37) Gts on 15.9.2016 and on the same day the sale consideration of the land compensation amount also paid to them vide Banker Cheque No.627889 Dt.
15.9.2016, for Rs.255000-00 and Ch. No. 627890 Dt. 15.9.2016 for Rs.29,55,000-00 respectively."

5. This Court after having considered the counter affidavit filed by the respondent No.2 having prima-facie felt that there is a deliberate violation of the order passed by this Court on 26.09.2016,
passed the following order dated 02.12.2022:
Dasyam Muralidhar vs Sri D. Ronald Rose, on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59621728/
1 3 MSK,J C.C.No.387 OF 2017 "Perused the counter affidavit and the reply.

sentences.text: It is noticed that the cheques were issued for payment of compensation on 15.09.2016.
According to learned counsel for the petitioner and reply affidavit, the sale deed in favour of the Government was executed on 15.10.2016.

As the amount is shown to have been paid much prior to the execution of the sale deed in favour of the Government, this Court entertains a doubt about the veracity of the contents of the counter affidavit filed by the respondents.

In the circumstances, the learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition is directed to place on record, the record pertaining to the payment of amount on 15.09.2016 and the copies of the sale deed executed in favour of the Government in respect of the subject property by the next date of hearing.

6. Thereafter, the matter underwent several adjournments and finally it was on 25.01.2023, the respondent No.2 filed additional counter affidavit admitting that the petitioner has submitted representation dated 29.09.2016, by which date, the cheques were already disbursed to the respondent Nos.3 and 4 for payment of compensation in respect of land in question and thereafter respondent No.2 got enquired into the matter through revenue officials and came to the conclusion that the land, which is sought to be acquired, belongs to respondent Nos.3 and 4 and further stated that by the date of receipt of order dated 27.09.2016 by the respondent No.2, the sale deeds executed by the respondent Nos.3 and 4 have already been presented before the concerned Registrar for registration and in view of the fact that huge extent of more than 5000 acres was being acquired,
the registration of the documents took 4 MSK,J C.C.No.387 OF 2017 considerable time and finally the documents were registered on 05.10.2016 and the cheques were duly encashed by the respondent Nos.3 and 4 on 06.10.2016.

The relevant portion from the said counter affidavit reads as follows:
"In response to the Para No.3 & 4 of the affidavit, it is respectfully submitted that the petitioner has submitted representations on 29.09.2016 and 25.01.2017 i.e., after distribution of land compensation cheque, for providing land compensation to the Yellu Srinivas Reddy and Yellu Jyothi for the suit land.

The Respondent No.2 has considered the petitioner's representations and instructed the revenue officials to re-verify the revenue records and physical enquiry to submit the detail report on the suit land.
As per the higher officer, the revenue officials re-verified revenue records and title and conducted field enquiry in the said numbers.

As per re- verification of revenue records and physical possession the land to an extent of Ac.0.05, 0.12 gts in Sy.No.758, 678 belongs to Yellu Srinivas Reddy and the land to an extent of Ac.3.22,
0.22, 0.33 gts in Sy.No.532, 758, 834 belongs to Yellu Jyothi.
The same names were reflected in the pahani from the year 2010- 11.
The Respondent No.2 considered the petitioner's application and replied the same, orally.

It is to state further that prior to distribution of compensation, the Dasyam Muralidhar vs Sri D. Ronald Rose, on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59621728/
2 register action of the lands as per G.O.Ms.No.123, village level teams along with sub-registrar and revenue officials were constituted to prepare the documents.

sentences.text: Similarly documentation were prepared in respect of the lands to an extent of Ac.5574.08 gts.
The documents were prepared on 05.09.2016.
Thereafter, the documents were submitted to the Registrar Office.
But after collecting all documents from 05.09.2016 by the Registrar Office but they have struck the date and numbered in October month.

Therefore, it is humbly submitted that my part of submitting the documents were completed on 05.09.2016, but as they were hundreds of documents they have numbered it on later stage, i.e., on 05.10.2016."
7.

From the counter affidavit and the additional counter affidavit together with the material filed along with the same and also after having considered the registered documents that were executed by respondent Nos.3 and 4 in respect of the subject land, this Court noticed that the said sale deeds were 5 MSK,J C.C.No.387 OF 2017 shown to have been executed on 05.10.2016 and the same were also registered on the same date and the cheques were issued in favour of the respondent Nos.3 and 4 though were shown to have been dated 15.09.2016 as is evident from the copies of the cheques filed before this Court, the date of said cheques were mentioned as 05.10.2016 in the registered sale deeds and the said cheques were encashed by respondent Nos.3 and 4 on 06.10.2016.

Thus, the registration of the documents and encashment of the cheques, disbursement of the compensation in favour of respondent Nos.3 and 4 had taken place only after the order passed by this Court on 27.09.2016.

As already noted above, the respondent No.2 herein has come to know about the order dated 27.09.2016 on 29.09.2016 and he should have taken immediate steps either for stopping disbursement of compensation or prevent the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 from encashing the said cheques.

Any simple attempt on the part of the respondent No.2 would have prevented respondent Nos.3 and 4 from encashing the said cheques resulting in disbursement of the compensation contrary to the order passed by this Court on 27.09.2016.
But the respondent No.2 failed to take any such positive action inspite of having knowledge about the order passed by this Court.
6 MSK,J C.C.No.387 OF 2017 8.
Such an action on the part of respondent No.2 certainly can be considered to be contumacious making him liable for all the consequences thereof.

But taking into consideration the fact that respondent No.2 was for acquiring huge extent of Ac.5574.08 guntas, which includes the subject land and all the documents were stated to have been presented for registration on 05.09.2016 itself,
but the process of registration took long time for registration of the documents including the sale deeds in question in respect of subject property, this Court is of the considered view that though there is no positive attempt made by the respondent No.2 to comply with the order passed by this court, there is no deliberate violation of the order passed by this Court by respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 appears to have acted in routine manner, while dealing with execution and registration of number of sale deeds covering an extent of Ac.5574.08 guntas.

9. Further, from the perusal of the affidavit filed by the petitioner in support of W.P.No.32684 of 2016, it is noticed that the petitioner is making claim over the subject land through her grandmother and there is dispute about the entitlement or otherwise of the petitioner to claim compensation over Dasyam Muralidhar vs Sri D. Ronald Rose, on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59621728/
3 the 7 MSK,J C.C.No.387 OF 2017 subject land and also the fact that revenue records reveal the names of respondent Nos.3 and 4 as pattadars in respect of the subject land.

sentences.text: The main Writ Petition is still pending for consideration before this Court on merits.

Taking into consideration of the fact that respondent No.2 has already retired from service, this Court is not inclined to proceed further in the matter especially in the context of the fact that respondent No.2 has filed an affidavit offering unconditional apology.

The relevant paragraph from the said affidavit filed by the respondent No.2 reads as under:
"I respectfully submitted that, in fact during the said period, I was the Revenue Divisional Officer on extension of my tenure after my retirement (I have retired on 31.08.2016).
During the relevant time about an extension of Ac.5574.08 gts.
Of land was requisitioned for acquisition for the purpose of Kaleshwaram Project (Mallannasagar Reservoir).
Therefore, I could not pay my full attention on the present subject matter and that had led to in encashment of the cheque.
In fact, I should have been more careful and addressed a letter to the banker for stop payment of the cheque amounts, after I received the order copy of this Hon'ble Court on 29th September, 2016.
I submit my unconditional apology for the above said lapse on my part and I request this Hon'ble Court to accept my apology and take a lenient view in the matter.
I undertake, that I would be more careful, henceforth, in discharging my function and in upholding the majesty of the Hon'ble Court and its orders."
10. In the light of the above, the Contempt Case is closed.

However, the compensation that was already paid in favour of respondent Nos.3 and 4 shall be subject to the further orders to be passed by this court in W.P.No.32684 of 2016 and in case finally the petitioner is found to be entitled for payment of 8 MSK,J C.C.No.387 OF 2017 compensation either in the pending Writ Petition or otherwise, the State shall first pay such compensation to the petitioner and then take steps for recovery of the amount paid to respondent Nos.3 and 4.
11.
Accordingly, the Contempt Case is closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous applications, if any, pending shall stand closed.
MUMMINENI SUDHEER KUMAR, J 16.06.2023 AS/MS 9 MSK,J C.C.No.387 OF 2017 THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE MUMMINENI SUDHEER KUMAR CONTEMPT CASE No.387 OF 2017 Dated:16.06.2023 AS/
